text:
Maya S: Customer reported multiple streaming sessions being billed as 5xx when the client cancels mid-stream. They say tokens were charged and dashboard shows 5xx spike. Request IDs: rq_0a1b2c3d, rq_0a1b2c3e.
Ben (Support): Thanks — do we have gateway logs for those request IDs? Any 'write error: broken pipe' or similar?
Maya S: Pasted the gateway excerpt: 
```
2026-03-10T14:22:01Z gateway INFO req=rq_0a1b2c3d status=200 streaming=true bytes_sent=4096
2026-03-10T14:22:02Z gateway ERROR req=rq_0a1b2c3d write_err="broken pipe" downstream_rst=true
2026-03-10T14:22:02Z billing INFO req=rq_0a1b2c3d classified=5xx tokens_billed=321
```
Ben (Support): So gateway marked as error and billing pipeline picked up as 5xx. Customer says client aborted after receiving first chunk; they expect client_cancel/harmless.
Elaine (SRE): Quick hypothesis: our halfclose/FIN handling currently maps any downstream socket error during write to 5xx. We should distinguish ECONNRESET/EOF vs application-level error.
Carlos (Eng-runtime): Can you share a minimal repro curl? We'll try to reproduce locally.
Maya S: Repro command customer used (JS): 
```
const r = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body: promptStream });
setTimeout(() => r.body.cancel(), 350); // abort after first chunk
```
Maya S: Also shared curl hack: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream" -d @payload.json --no-buffer --max-time 2
```
DeployBot: Trace created: https://trace.redwood.ai/trace/rq_0a1b2c3d (shows downstream FIN followed by write error) :robot_face:
Elaine (SRE): I ran a repro and saw the same: gateway log shows write to socket fails with EPIPE, then our error handler sets http status to 502 and emits billing.event=5xx_count.
Carlos (Eng-runtime): Ok — short-term: we can change billing classifier to look for downstream_rst or client_fin and map to client_abort before counting as 5xx. Long-term: fix runtime to surface a "client_disconnected" flag to the control plane.
Ben (Support): Customer wants refund for billed tokens on those requests. Do we have reliable way to detect these now?
TelemetryBot: Metric query: billing.billing_events{type:5xx,code:502}.rollup(1h) shows 4x spike aligned to customer's activity window. Filtering by trace tag downstream_rst reduces to 0 for that customer.
Maya S: Proposed action: 1) Manually refund the affected request IDs, 2) Add a short-lived billing rule to ignore requests with downstream_rst for that account, 3) Post a P2 to eng-runtime to add explicit client_abort signal.
Carlos (Eng-runtime): I'll own the P2. Implementation plan: emit explicit event via control-plane RPC when runtime sees EOF/FIN before final chunk, and add a safe heuristic to avoid counting those as 5xx. Will require a small schema change and a migration for old events. ETA: 3 days for hotfix + 2 weeks for robust fix.
Elaine (SRE): For monitoring, I'll add a dashboard to surface write_err + downstream_rst rate and a paging alert if write_err spikes for >5m.
Ben (Support): I'll open a billing ticket and process refunds for rq_0a1b2c3d,e and any others the customer lists. Maya, can you confirm which additional request_ids they have?
Maya S: Sent them a request for a compact list. Also asked for client-side logs (browser/SDK) to confirm they indeed abort.
Carlos (Eng-runtime): Quick note for repro: using curl with --no-buffer + a client that sends FIN immediately after first chunk reproduces it. Code snippet we used to reproduce server-side: 
```
// pseudo
streamer.write(firstChunk);
// client closes connection
onWriteError(err) { if (err.code === 'EPIPE' || err.code === 'ECONNRESET') markClientAbort(); else markGatewayError(); }
```
Maya S: Customer replied with 6 request_ids, confirmed they used the JS fetch abort pattern.
Ben (Support): Thanks team. Next steps: refunds processed (billing), short-term classifier rule applied, P2 created and assigned to Carlos. I'll follow up with the customer tonight. :white_check_mark:
